title: Rehousing a dirty AND with wires fails: in some AND/OR edge circuit, zeroing it and serving lost edges by stars and wire-widened tops exceeds the count

plain_statement: False: G a graph, F its edge function, C AND/OR (two earlier wires each, so only earlier wires) for F, g a dirty AND. Zero g; each lost edge is served by a star x_c AND OR(O c), c in St an end; or by a top T in Tp (AND below F, ORs to the output) widened by wires U(T) earlier than T, not g, T's other operand AND u below F, both true there. Dd: gates nobody reads; Fo: gates reading wires the zero forces false; k: tops whose widened operand is so forced. Then F has an AND/OR circuit with fewer dirty ANDs and at most |C| - 1 - |Dd| - |Fo| - k + sum_St (|O c| + 1) + sum_Tp |U(T)| gates.
